subject: Discovery recap: Inference cost pressure & next steps (Finbot)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finbot.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: Inference cost pressure & next steps (Finbot)

Alex — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our conversation so we have alignment and clear next steps. Feel free to reply with edits.

Key pain points you shared:
- Unit economics are currently the top blocker — your team is seeing token-level costs that make scaling new features unaffordable.
- Tail latency spikes during peak (batching windows) are causing poor UX for some flows.
- Current stack: hosted open-source models on AWS (g5 + self-managed autoscaling, minimal KV caching). No quantization in prod.

Goals / success criteria
- Reduce per-token inference cost by ~40–60% while maintaining current output quality.
- P95 latency under 200ms for user-facing generators; 99th percentile tolerable up to 350ms for batch jobs.
- Support for batching/caching without materially increasing latency.
- Openness to model quantization (4-bit) if quality stays acceptable in evals.

What Redwood can help with (high level)
- Dedicated inference profiles (batching + KV/prefix caching) to lower unit costs.
- Quantized model variants with kernel/compile optimizations for throughput and latency.
- Migration path: small pilot on 1–2 models, engineering sync to define telemetry and acceptance tests, then a 2–4 week POC.

Proposed next steps
1) Engineering sync (30–45m) to scope POC and agree success metrics — proposed Wed Feb 18, 10:00–11:00 PT.
2) Redwood to share a preliminary cost estimate and mutual action plan (attached).
3) If procurement needs to be involved, loop in Sara or your procurement alias so we can surface contract/terms early (Ben will coordinate).

Attachments: redwood-map-20260218.pdf (1-page mutual action plan), finbot-cost-estimate-20260218.xlsx (sample unit-cost model)

If this looks good I’ll send a calendar invite for Wednesday and Ben will include procurement language.

Thanks — looking forward to partnering on this,

— Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference — Production-first inference runtime

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finbot.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Inference cost pressure & next steps (Finbot)

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear notes. High level: all captured and the goals look right. A few clarifications:
- The 40–60% target is what we’d need to make the new personalization features viable; 50% would be a win.
- On quantization: our ML team is willing to test 4-bit for non-critical pipelines, but we’ll need to validate against our QA prompt set first.

I’ll loop Sara (procurement) on this thread so she’s aware of timelines; she’ll also confirm whether we need an NDA before a cost spreadsheet exchange.

Wed 10:00 PT works for our engineers. Please send the invite.

— Alex

- Please have an owner from your ML infra team who can speak to current batching windows and how request routing works (prefix vs whole-request caching).
- We’ll bring a short checklist for success metrics (token-level cost baseline, a 10k prompt eval set for quality regression, latency SLOs), and a quick runbook for the POC (models, dataset slices, telemetry).

Attached the one-pager mutual action plan and a sample cost model (estimates are illustrative and will be refined after the sync).
